subject: Evaluation & Ramp Playbook — DataForge MAP and Renewal Triggers
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@dataforge.ai>

Cc: Ethan Chung <ethan.chung@dataforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Trial evaluation + timeline for production ramp

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profiles and the quantized footprint look promising. Our team is keen to run a short evaluation (3 weeks) and then plan a phased ramp to a small production footprint. Before we kick off, can you share: 1) a sample mutual action plan (high-level milestones + owner matrix), 2) any guidelines on commit sizing to qualify for ramp discounts, and 3) typical SOC2 evidence you can provide during evaluation?

We'd like to align on a close timeline (trial -> pilot -> contract) that fits our Q4 roadmap. Target close: end of October, but flexible if we can show concrete MAP milestones.

Best,
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataForge AI

Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@dataforge.ai>, Ethan Chung <ethan.chung@dataforge.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation + timeline for production ramp

Sara — thanks for the note and great to hear the team found the demo useful. I attached a working MAP (DataForge_MAP_v1.pdf) and a short SOC2 summary for the evaluation period. High level:

- Week 0–1 (Evaluation): Sandbox onboarding, performance baseline tests, and targeted prompt set validation (owner: DataForge / Redwood SE).
- Week 2 (Pilot): Throughput tests with production traffic replay; KV/cache tuning and batching profile locked (owner: DataForge / Redwood Ops).
- Week 36 (Ramp): Commit sizing and reserved capacity proposal; start of discounted committed throughput once commit accepted (owner: DataForge procurement / Redwood sales).

Commit/discount guidance (rough):
- < 50k tokens/day: no commit — pay-as-you-go.
- 50k200k tokens/day: 6-month commit -> 10% discount at 50k baseline, additional 5% at 100k baseline.
- >200k tokens/day: 12-month reserved capacity -> tiered discounts up to 20% depending on burst policies.

Suggested close timeline: if evaluation starts 10/5, pilot concluded by 10/19, we can put a committed proposal + SOW in front of procurement by 10/22 and target signature by 10/30. If you need an earlier signature to secure capacity, we can provision a canary reserved pool with a short-term ramp commitment.

I've cc'd Marcus and Dev from pricing/engineering to the thread so they can weigh in on the discount bands and operational ramp feasibility.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Chung <ethan.chung@dataforge.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@dataforge.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation + timeline for production ramp

Thanks Hannah 94 this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifying items from our side before we start:

1) Can you confirm SLA expectations during the pilot (p99)?
2) We favor a 6-week overall cadence: 2 weeks eval, 2 weeks pilot, 2 weeks ramp validation. Will that change the discount thresholds?
3) Procurement will want to know whether the discount bands can be staged based on observed throughput at the end of each 2-week block rather than an upfront baseline.

If that approach works we can accelerate the signature because our finance lead is more comfortable with staged commits.

-Ethan
Product Ops, DataForge
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Chung <ethan.chung@dataforge.ai>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation + timeline for production ramp

Ethan 94 good questions. Short answers inline below, and Marcus/Dev please confirm operational and pricing feasibility.

> 1) SLA expectations during the pilot (p99)?
We can commit to a 200ms p90 and a 600ms p99 for the pilot on our hosted tier with the recommended model variant and autoscaling policy. If you need stronger p99 SLOs we can propose a dedicated pool in the SOW (cost delta included).

> 2) 6-week cadence vs. 4-week?
We can support 6 weeks; numbers below assume the staged model you suggest (evaluation -> pilot -> ramp validation). Staged commits are fine and align with Redwood Optimize workflows.

> 3) Staged discount bands?
We can structure a 3-step ramp:
- Stage A (post-eval): 30-day trial usage credits + commitment option to lock a 6-week pilot baseline (no discount yet).
- Stage B (after pilot): if throughput >= X tokens/day for 7 consecutive days, trigger Tier 1 (10% discount) for the next 3 months.
- Stage C (after ramp validation): if throughput meets the Tier 2 baseline, switch to reserved pricing with longer-term discount (1218% depending on commit length).

Marcus / Dev — can we confirm: 1) the technical gating metric (X tokens/day) we should use as the Tier 1 trigger; 2) whether a rolling 7-day lookback is feasible; and 3) a recommended buffer for capacity provisioning so we don't throttle during burst windows?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial evaluation + timeline for production ramp

Hannah / Dev 94 quick pricing ops note:

We can support the staged discount design. Suggested gating metrics (practical and easy to audit):
- Tier 1 trigger: sustained 7-day average of 75k tokens/day (rolling).
- Tier 2 trigger: sustained 14-day average of 180k tokens/day.

Capacity buffer: provision an extra 25% headroom on reserved pools for the first 30 days after a stage flip to absorb warm-up variability. We will also enable prefix KV caching for replayed traffic to reduce cold-start token costs during pilot validation.

Commercial terms to offer DataForge (recommended):
- Pilot Addendum: 30-day evaluation credit (up to $3k) + staged commit option.
- Ramp Addendum: conditional 3-month Tier 1 discount (10%) upon hitting Tier 1. If Tier 2 is achieved, convert remaining months to reserved capacity pricing with an extra 5% uplift off list.

I'll draft the short SOW/term sheet and route for legal review. Dev: confirm capacity buffer and KV cache toggle plan.

-Marcus
VP, Commercial Ops
marcus.lin@redwood.com
